description.value: The Museum of Anthropology at UBC is one of Canada's premier anthropology museums, holding an internationally significant collection of Northwest Coast First Nations art including monumental totem poles and ceremonial objects. Perched on the cliffs of Point Grey overlooking the Strait of Georgia, it is housed in a landmark modernist building and draws visitors from around the world. Touring cyclists can reach it via a scenic coastal route along NW Marine Drive, though the museum's own website cautions that the approach involves a significant hill.

No bike parking infrastructure (racks, covered storage) is mentioned anywhere in the website content despite cycling being listed as an arrival mode — this required criterion could not be confirmed.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: A world-class cultural destination on the UBC campus reachable via a scenic coastal cycling route; a natural and notable stop for touring cyclists exploring Vancouver's west side.
